name: Cross-origin isolation and SharedArrayBuffer clocks
plain: Sites that send COOP and COEP headers unlock finer timers and SharedArrayBuffer.
meaning: Gives a page a 5 microsecond clock and shared memory, both needed for wasm threads. A worker counter on SharedArrayBuffer is a high resolution clock that also powers Spectre-class attacks.

steps: Use SharedArrayBuffer and performance.now at finer resolution

limits.headline: Can use a very fine clock and shared memory, but only if the site opts in
limits.user_action: Nothing. The site sets special page headers when it loads
can: Get a clock down to about 5 microseconds
Share memory between its own background workers
Run heavier tools such as WebAssembly threads
Use these also for very precise timing attacks
cannot: Get these without the special page headers
Load some outside content like ads and embeds freely
limits.reach_label: Only when the site opts in

story.what_it_is: Sites that send two special headers unlock very precise timers and shared memory for heavy apps.

marketing.name: Cross origin isolation guide
marketing.pitch: Google explains how to turn on isolation so a page can use powerful features like shared memory safely.

marketing.name: Why COOP and COEP
marketing.pitch: Explains that isolation makes powerful features safe because it blocks risky mixing with other sites.

story.for_you: You do not choose or see this. Heavy web apps like big games or video editors run faster in a tab, because the site proved it is walled off from others.
story.for_makers: Isolation unlocks threads, shared memory and finer timers, which are needed for fast code. The cost is that the site must prove all content it loads is safe, which can be hard with ads and embeds.

use_cases.example: A big web game built with Unity or Unreal uses several threads in a tab, which needs isolation to run well.
A browser video tool like ffmpeg.wasm runs faster with shared memory.
A code editor in the browser runs a whole dev server in a tab using threads.
A web DAW processes many audio tracks at once on several threads without crackles.
A design or spreadsheet app runs heavy calculations on many threads in the browser.
Researchers use finer timers to study side channel attacks, which is why browsers wall these timers off.
A browser based coding class runs Python in a tab with shared memory so lessons feel fast.

risks: Makes timing attacks easier if misused

technical_bounds: Isolation blocks embedding non-CORP cross-origin content
Not available in iframes without allow and the same headers

value.abuse: Enables micro-timing side channels in a compromised cross-origin context

history.change: SAB re-enabled for cross-origin isolated pages
